question: Under the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act, how long can a Chapter 7 bankruptcy remain on your credit report?
true_claim_text: a Chapter 7 bankruptcy can stay on a credit report for up to 10 years
false_claim_text: a Chapter 7 bankruptcy falls off a credit report after 7 years
source: Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681c(a)(1) (CFPB guidance): a bankruptcy case may be reported for up to 10 years from the date of entry of the order for relief or the date of adjudication (in a voluntary case this coincides with the filing date); the 7-year limit applies to most other negative items.
